Phase III / Fizz Free flavors ACV
Net revenue benefit (Alani; pull-forward from Q1)
Aluminum - Middle East share of global production
fully baked in by end March 2026
54% of Liquid Refresher Beverage growth comes out of energy; 85% of energy growth is sugar-free - energy remains the biggest growth driver in beverage.
Convenience single consumption is the main driver of growth for both brands, especially Alani.

Brand Celsius scanner softened in early Q1 2026 from a deliberate SKU rationalization ('trimming the tail' of least-productive SKUs) and lapping four Q1 2025 flavor launches with zero launches in Q1 2026 - not a health issue.
Celsius innovation layers on in Q2, Q3, Q4 2026 after zero Q1 launches; multiple Celsius LTOs planned plus potential back-half non-LTO innovation.
Watch the top 10-15 Celsius SKUs rise in ACV over the next ~8 weeks as the SKU rationalization plays out ('fast cars on the track').

No significant change in Celsius/Alani crossover-consumer data over 12 months despite Alani's triple-digit growth - the brands taste completely different and serve different consumers; Alani is incremental, not cannibalistic.
Essentials (16-oz format) has been a little bit of a drag; a work in progress expected to improve through the year - company not giving up on the format.

The $25M Q4 net benefit is a pull-forward out of Q1 into Q4 - Cherry Bomb LTO (a Q1 scanner phenomenon) was loaded into Pepsi in December; that revenue captured in December, absent from Q1. Cautious against expecting additional pipe-fill.
Celsius scanner now looks very similar to the sell-in to Pepsi; Alani days-on-hand expected to stay roughly linear (a function of sell-through), mitigating inventory swings.
Pepsi captaincy lets Celsius be the insights/growth/marketing engine of the energy category while Pepsi provides world-class DSD; manages planograms for Pepsi-controlled coolers nationwide.

Alani LTO success is about brand health and lifting the totality of the brand - LTOs address frequency in the existing base and recruit new users; three early-2025 LTOs (Cotton Candy, Sherbet Swirl, Strawberry Sunrise) became permanent SKUs.
Cotton Candy is now the top-performing Alani SKU at only 40% ACV - significant upside; some LTOs (Witch's Brew, Winter Wonderland) are seasonal and not expected off-season.
Coordinated multi-brand LTO cadence in 2026 so one of the three brands is always on promotion with minimal overlap - 2025 had preset Alani cadence causing overlap; expect Alani LTOs to be bigger.
Alani has massive opportunity - outpaced expectations; planogram resets occur January through May, so the company has 'barely scratched the surface'; Alani under-served in regions like New York City.
Rockstar 2026 is a stabilization year - rationalize SKUs, refocus on a more male-heavy 16-oz consumer; goal is to get the business back into growth; brand incremental, different demographic.

International is a huge global opportunity - Celsius Holdings at ~5% international vs. #2 player at ~40%; ramp builds over 3-5 years; Iberia launched March 2026; evaluating concentrate/license/franchise models alongside premium finished-goods.
Same macro trends global - sugar-free growing, female consumer growing, functional beverage growing in all markets entered.

Gross margin stair-steps Q1 to Q2 to back half (low 50s) - Q4 2025 carried one-time scrap/returns/freight from the old-to-new distribution transition; Alani baked into orbit model end of March, Rockstar a quarter behind.

Aluminum/tariff increases kicked in back half of 2025, so 2026 partly rolls over that step-up rather than absorbing incremental cost; company does not currently source from the Middle East; 2027+ new capacity should more than offset.

Multi-brand price-pack-promotion strategy enables RGM 'from an exponential level' - Alani as super premium, Celsius as premium, Rockstar as premium economy; promote against the competition, not on top of each other.
No correlation found between gas prices/foot traffic and energy sales; foot traffic up in January/February; first couple of months of 2026 great for both brands.
Capital allocation: invest in business growth (including international), pay down ~$700M debt, share buyback ($40M spent Q4, $260M remaining); M&A on the table if value-additive.
S&M expected to stay 22-24% of revenue (not slowing investment - highly competitive space, private competitor 'dumping' money in); G&A and promotional allowances are scale-leverage opportunities.
Long-term gross margin drivers: cost of materials, freight lanes, tolling charges, second production line, vertical integration, RGM via promotional-pack strategy - clear line of sight to mid-50s GM.
Expected energy category growth in 2026 and how quickly the industry can close the household-penetration gap.

No public category-growth view, but (per Mintel etc.) energy will continue to be the biggest beverage/CPG driver - pivoted from impulse to a daily lifestyle routine; 54% of LRB growth from energy, 85% of energy growth sugar-free; Celsius portfolio well positioned to grow.
Whether higher gas prices/uneasy consumer affected convenience-channel volumes, and history of gas-price impact.

First couple of months of 2026 great for both brands; convenience a huge opportunity for Alani and Celsius (singles a strong Celsius driver ~six months). Multiple reports (one from UBS) found no correlation between gas prices/foot traffic and sales; foot traffic up Jan/Feb; energy continues to grow.
Whether growth is still sourced from adjacent categories and new consumers rather than category leaders.

Energy still sourcing strongly from RTD and drip coffee (coffee players conditioned cold-caffeine consumption); retailers shrinking the beer case to allocate space to energy; sourcing from hydration, coffee, premium water across many occasions.
Explain the PepsiCo category captaincy, how it differs from operations several years ago, the biggest tangible benefits, and summer-season unlocks.

Entered the Pepsi system in 2022; captaincy strengthens the partnership - Celsius acts as the insights/growth/marketing engine while Pepsi provides world-class DSD. Delivers priority periods and planogram management for Pepsi-controlled coolers nationwide; 'focus and structure so we can win together.'

What management learned about Celsius/Alani overlap given slowing core Celsius growth while Alani accelerates; why core trends weakened, Essentials underperformance, and whether this is a sign of things to come as comps harden.

Crossover-consumer data showed no significant change over 12 months; products taste completely different, different female consumers. Core softness reflects a deliberate SKU rationalization - trimming the tail, lifting top-SKU ACV (low 80s toward mid-90s) and mid-50s flavors toward 80%+ - and lapping four Q1 2025 launches with zero in Q1 2026, with innovation layering in Q2-Q4. Brand is healthy (over 20% convenience growth most months); Essentials drag does not reflect Celsius's health.
Why Essentials has been weaker and how committed the company is to the brand.

The 16-oz Essentials format serves a slightly different consumer and is important; company wants to avoid it being seen as just a value brand. A work in progress expected to improve through the year - 'certainly not giving up' on the format; confident in brand Celsius's health.
The core Celsius innovation pipeline - Fizz Free and flavors - and what investors should watch for.

Phase III (non-carbonated Fizz Free line) is more a marketing campaign than true innovation, cycling SKUs to build TDP - two flavors launched last year sit at ~30% ACV with room to grow. Innovation is about cadence: as the Alani lime slush LTO winds down a Celsius LTO appears, then Alani, then Celsius - minimizing overlap. 2026 designed so one of the three brands is always on promotion with minimal overlap.
Key learnings from the Celsius LTO strategy and how they inform the go-forward approach.

Alani's LTO success shows LTOs are about brand health and lifting the totality of the brand, not just the spike. The first Celsius LTO (Spritz Vibe) was a chance to 'dip our toe in the water' before migrating a line to Pepsi; Cherry Bomb for Alani was a successful follow-on. Expect Alani LTOs bigger (community more accustomed), but Celsius LTOs can still drive success and lift the portfolio.
The Alani Nu LTO strategy and what it does to the broader franchise; how LTOs become permanent SKUs.

Alani LTOs create community excitement (consumers videotaping themselves wiping out inventory on TikTok), drive frequency in the existing base and recruit new users - Cotton Candy drove incredible excitement. Three early-2025 LTOs relaunched permanently; Cotton Candy now the top portfolio SKU at only 40% ACV. LTO-to-permanent decisions driven by velocity, consumer feedback, and SKU/ACV expansion opportunity; some LTOs (Witch's Brew, Winter Wonderland) are seasonal.
How Alani Nu's performance compares to expectations and how to frame growth going forward given harder comps.

Alani has massive opportunity and outpaced expectations - could reach a 9 or 10 share but not in under 12 months, mostly without the full power of the Pepsi system (only a couple of months). Planogram resets occur January-May, so 'barely scratched the surface'; Alani under-served in regions like New York City, strong in the central US - substantial future runway.
Specifics on LTOs into the summer selling season - number, size versus last year - and how Celsius and Alani LTO strategies are balanced.

Do not believe Reddit speculation on LTO dates. Expect a similar number of Alani LTOs to 2025 (possible slight modification); for Celsius - which had only one LTO in 2025 - multiple LTOs in 2026, designed to drive frequency, generate excitement, recruit/re-recruit users. Potential back-half non-LTO innovation for Celsius; program expected to uplift the entire portfolio.
With both brands gaining share, whether there is a world where Alani has a larger energy-drink share than Celsius.

Brands are close on share now; encouraging path for Alani. Company moved from a single brand to a portfolio and manages for total portfolio health - growing Celsius and Alani, flattening Rockstar before regrowing. Celsius's goal is to get back to and exceed category growth, with foundational Q1 work and innovation layering. ~20 share 'is certainly not where we expect to finish the year.'
The Rockstar opportunity and what success looks like a year from now.

2026 for Rockstar is about stabilizing the business - rationalizing SKUs, focusing on core SKUs that drive sales and the core male-heavy 16-oz consumer. Goal is to get Rockstar back into growth; the brand is incremental, targeting a different demographic. Company has people who built Rockstar and is going back to the tactics that 'made Rockstar, Rockstar.'
Update on the international strategy, takeaways from new markets like the UK, and how the company decides to make international a bigger priority.

A ton of white space - #2 player ~40% international vs. Celsius Holdings ~5%. A new international leader (~four months in) is formalizing the global expansion plan, tweaked by the Alani/Rockstar acquisitions. Near-term focus is integrating those businesses and capturing the ~17% Celsius / 100%+ Alani shelf gains; larger international push builds over 3-5 years. Evaluating concentrate/license/franchise models; launched Iberia in March 2026.
Whether the US energy dynamics (zero sugar, health/wellness, female/older consumers) represent the same opportunity outside the US.

Absolutely - in all markets entered or evaluated, sugar-free is growing, the female consumer is growing, functional beverage is growing, driven by the same macro trends of healthy, better-for-you, functional, great-tasting energy.
$25M Net Inventory Benefit & Alani Reported vs. Tracked Growth

Whether quarter-to-date shipments still in line with consumption (re the $25M Q4 benefit), how to think about Alani reported vs. tracked growth, and whether the prior inventory-correction dynamic could repeat.

Celsius scanner now looks very similar to the sell-in to Pepsi. For Alani, the ~$25M Q4 net benefit is 'a pull forward out of Q1 into Q4' - the Cherry Bomb LTO (a Q1 scanner phenomenon) loaded into Pepsi in December, revenue captured in December, won't appear in Q1; big bulk of the $25M. Cautious against expecting additional pipe-fill; days-on-hand should stay roughly linear. Cited four years of Pepsi-system experience, Eric Hansen (26 yrs with Pepsi) as President, two new Pepsi-affiliated board members, and the captaincy - does not anticipate a repeat of the prior dynamic.
Remind investors of the first-half vs. second-half gross margin phasing and what gives confidence in another year of margin expansion.

Stair-step approach from Q4 - improving through Q1, Q2, back into the low 50s in the back half. Q4 2025 carried one-time scrap/returns/freight from the old-to-new distribution transition. Alani fully baked into the orbit model by end of March; by Q2 the baked-in Alani margin profile applies; Rockstar a quarter behind (acquired Aug 28, 2025), fully integrated by end Q2; back half benefits from orbit-model freight savings and supply-chain/scale raw-material savings.
How management manages aluminum / Midwest premium exposure going forward while integrating the two acquired brands.

Alani and Rockstar pulled fully into Celsius's contracts/supply chain, so the same tactics apply and scale delivers savings to offset aluminum/tariffs. Aluminum/tariff increases kicked in back half 2025, so 2026 partly rolls over that step-up. Short-term Middle East uncertainty (~9% of global aluminum production; company does not currently source there) but comfortable short-term; 2027-2028 new capacity should more than offset, with levers available.
How management thinks about pricing and promo optimization for the Celsius portfolio in 2026 given more active competitive pricing, and balancing pricing against brand momentum.

2026 planning very different from the historical single-brand approach - the portfolio enables a multi-brand price-pack-promotion strategy and RGM 'from an exponential level.' Core principles: don't promote on top of each other, promote against the competition. Positioning Alani as super premium, Celsius as premium, Rockstar as premium economy; pricing by channel, retailer, demographic, region.
The two or three most important drivers to get from current gross margin to target, and how quickly the mid-50s gross margin can be achieved.

Reiterated the 'handful of years' timeline for the mid-50s. Drivers: cost of materials, freight lanes, tolling charges with manufacturers; a second production line online back half 2026 (Q4) adding margin/efficiency from running two lines in one plant; vertical-integration COGS savings; and RGM as a big margin opportunity via the promotional-pack strategy.
The right level of sales-and-marketing investment as the business matures into a multi-brand portfolio, and where the most efficiency opportunity lies.

Would not slow S&M investment given the highly competitive space (two biggest players invest heavily, private one 'dumping' money in) and the need to fuel growth. Historically S&M 22-24% of revenue, expected to stay in that neighborhood near-term, with continued investment in salespeople ('win in the streets'). G&A is a scale-leverage opportunity; promotional allowances (above the line) another area to improve margins.
How management thinks about capital allocation priorities as free cash flow normalizes with the Alani integration largely behind by midyear.

A high cash-generating business that will keep building cash. Priorities: invest in business growth (including turning up international investment as Garrett joins and the Dublin team scales); pay down ~$700M of debt; share buyback ($40M spent Q4, $260M remaining). M&A remains on the table opportunistically if value-additive.
